messages.subject: Error creating coverage layer
parts:
Hi everyone, 

My name is Sara and I'm trying to make a zig zag boat survey design in the sea (coastal survey), but this error is constantly appearing to me when I try to create the coverage layer. I'm sending the prt screen of the error attached.

I'm also sending the project I created for you to see if I did something wrong. The message of the error says that the data layer does not contain a valid polygon, but I've already imported the shapefile of the study area to the project folder and added the "Link ID" field in SIG (I followed the user manual's instructions) and I can see correctly the map layer of the study area in Map Tab.

Do you know what I am doing wrong?


Thank you in advance, 


Best regards, 


Sara

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error creating coverage layer
parts:
Dear Sara,


I notice in one of your images that a value of NULL is in the LinkID column... just checking that you set this to 1 before you imported it into Distance? That is one potential source of error.


Otherwise it is not uncommon for issues with vertices to arise when working with shapefiles... perhaps there is an ordering issue. I have had very bizarre things happening when working in GIS leading me to have to recreate my study are shapefile.


Please let me know if these two things do not resolve the issue.


Kind regards, Laura



Dr. L Marshall

Centre for Research into Ecological & Environmental Modelling

University of St. Andrews

Hi, 

 

thank you for your sugestions. With you I am not alone with Distance software xD.

 

I tried to do again my shapefile of the study area in GIS and import again to distance but the error message persisted.  What I did was extract the coordinates of the vertices of my shapefile in GIS and then I copied them to the table in Shape Properties window (that was empty before, since Distance has not processed the shape file properly) and then it worked! I managed to do my Coverage Layer (Grid) ad to create some designs!


In design survey I have some doubts when I'm defining the design in the Design Properties Window. In the Equal Angle ZigZag Design, how do I know the Effort Allocation I need? or in case I choose "Effort determined by sampler angle" how do I choose the appropriate angle for my survey?

 

In the Equal Spaced ZigZag design, how do I know the spacing I need beween transects? I'm making these questions because in the survey i'm trying to plan, the important things are: transects should be in zigzag (coastal boatsurvey) and I want to cover 3 to 5% of my study area. And don't have maximum width for my observations, I wanted to do post-truncation later, when analyzing the data. The sampler length or angle I didn't defined, cause it will be the necessary to cover my 3 to 5% of the study area. 


These statistics below are the ones that say what proportion of my study area am I sampling, right?


EXPECTED PROPORTION OF STRATUM SAMPLED: < 0.001

APPROXIMATED COVERAGE PROBABILITY FOR STRATUM: < 0.001



In Adjusted Angle ZigZag Design, when I press RUN the program stops working (don't respond) and I have to close the program. Perhaps I'm putting Coverage Proability too high? The coverage probability is what proportion I want to cover with my transects, right? which means 3-5%?
 

I'm sending my project attached to you since maybe you can detect something wrong in it more easily.


Another question: Is it possible to export the map with the transects and then put them into GIS software? Or the transects only?


Thank you in advance for the help. 

 

Best regards, 

 

 

Sara

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error creating coverage layer
parts:
Sara

Very impressive persistence on your part to get your study area into Distance.  Congratulations.

Now that you've gotten your shapefile into Distance and built your coverage grid; you are able to prepare your design.  Let me proceed through your questions.

- Effort allocation for equal angle design: often investigators have an idea of the amount of ship time or fuel they have in their budget.  Time or fuel can be converted to distances, which can be entered as "available effort."

- effort determined by sampler angle: the smaller the angle the closer together will be the legs of the zigzag.  the 'appropriate' angle would be determined by trial and error

- equal spaced zigzag spacing: determined by trial and error again; closer spacing of turnaround points will result in greater amount of effort

- "I want to cover 3 to 5% of my study area":  I take issue with this statement.  I'd be curious why this is a design criterion.  It is more appropriate to determine adequacy of a survey design based upon a) target precision of design or b) number of replicate transects (which helps determine the adequacy of estimating encounter rate variance).  Have a look through the sample size determination section either Buckland et al. (2015) or Buckland et al. (2001) or this pdf of Buckland et al. (1993)

http://distancesampling.org/downloads/distancebook1993/chapter7.pdf  Proportion of study area sampled is not a design criterion.  Quite good results can be accomplished with proportion of study area >1% under many circumstance.

- I too have trouble with the adjusted angle zigzag design.  Not only are they difficult for the design engine to compute, they are difficult to execute in the field (as the skipper is continuously changing heading).

- Finally, the coordinates of a design are provided at the end of a design engine run (on the page labelled sampler location list).  This is what you would give to the skipper or place into a GIS.  Here is an example:

messages.author: d6a29bde56bb826d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error creating coverage layer
parts:
Dear Sara,


Further to Eric's response, I have had a quick look at your project and E-mail again.


While it is not best practise to generate your survey based on a desired coverage probability it is indeed an option offered for the adjusted angle design so I will explain what was going wrong for you.


You stated in your E-mail that you do not have a maximum width for your observations so I see in your project that you left the sampler width as the default of 1m. However, Distance uses the sampler width to calculate the coverage - it needs to calculate the area covered by the samplers and then divide this by the total area of the study region. This is why Distance was struggling to generate your adjusted angle design... it would have needed to generate many many many of these extremely thin transects in order to achieve the 5% coverage that you requested and ends up hanging.


When you are assessing coverage (usually for the purposes of assessing whether you have uniform coverage probability) it is a good idea to look at past surveys and get an idea about a realistic truncation distance for the sampler width.


As per Eric's recommendation I would stick with the equal spaced zigzag design, I have also noticed that the adjusted angle is a bit temperamental when generating the transects. If you are concerned about the effects of the uneven coverage please take advantage of the simulation engine to reassure yourself that this design should only introduce minimal amounts of bias (if indeed any) to the density/abundance estimates. The exact effects will depend on your particular situation and this is exactly what the simulation engine was designed to assess.


I also note that you are using an older version of Distance so I would also recommend for using the simulation engine that you download Distance 7.2.


Best wishes, Laura


Dr. L Marshall

Centre for Research into Ecological & Environmental Modelling

University of St. Andrews

Tel: 01334 461808
